rationale:
The requirement `requirements.sdk.validation-cache.node_data` has two obligations. An assigned handle returns its data, and an unassigned integer returns `None`. Both are covered by the marked tests.

- **Assigned handle returns its data.** `crates/trust-but-verify/tests/contracts.rs#fn[clones_interning_the_same_data_concurrently_get_one_handle]` interns `Node(42)` from several cache clones. It asserts `cache.node_data(ids[0]).as_deref() == Some(&Node(42))`. That checks both the returned value and that it is the `Arc` payload of the shared handle. It also interns `Node(43)` and asserts the handle differs. `crates/trust-but-verify/tests/contracts.rs#fn[saved_node_and_edge_inputs_survive_a_different_handle_allocation_order]` adds more coverage through `durable_inputs`, which resolves handles with `node_data(..).unwrap()` and compares the results to expected node data. Many other domain helpers also call `node_data(..).unwrap()`, so lookup of assigned handles is exercised broadly.
- **Unassigned integer returns `None`.** The same second test builds a fresh `ValidationCache` and asserts `fresh.cache().node_data(subject).is_none()`. Here `subject` is a handle assigned in a different cache and not yet assigned in the fresh one. That is the unassigned case, and the test asserts the outcome directly.

The implementation is a single indexed lookup (`get_index(node.index).cloned()`), so there are no further branches. I read it only to see how the lookup works. The unassigned-handle case is checked on an empty cache, not as an out-of-range index on a populated one. The requirement does not distinguish those cases, so I do not count that as a gap. No {fixme} acknowledgments apply.

text: `node_data` returns the data associated with an assigned handle. An unassigned integer returns `None`.
pub fn node_data(&self, node: NodeId<D>) -> Option<Arc<D::NodeData>>;
